BiblicalUsage: Karah is to purchase — to buy food and drink in the wilderness, to provide for an enemy and send him home, to buy a wife back with silver and barley. Moses tells Israel to buy meat and water from the Edomites for money; Elisha makes a great provision for the Syrian raiders and sends them to their master; and Hosea buys back his wife for fifteen pieces of silver.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word runs straight to the cross: Hosea bought back a faithless wife, and God bought back a faithless people — and the price was not silver and barley but the blood of His Son. Fifteen pieces of silver bought a wife; the blood of Christ bought a people.
